Counsel for the petitioner : Sri Dasari S.V.V.S.V. Prasad

 Order

This writ petition is filed to declare the high handed action of the respondents in trying to lay the road from Machilipatnam- Challapalli Main R & B Road by encroaching upon the petitioner's land in an extent of Ac.2-50 cents in survey No.129/3 of Rudravaram village, Machilipatnam Mandal,
Krishna District, without following the provisions under the Right to Fair SRSJ Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013, as illegal and arbitrary.

entities.text: Right to Fair SRSJ Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013

sentences.text:
2. Heard Sri Dasari S.V.V.S.V.Prasad, learned counsel for the petitioner; Sri Bharat, learned Assistant Government Pleader for Revenue for respondent Nos.1, 2, 4, 6; Smt. Sravana Sandhya,
learned Assistant Government Pleader for Land Acquisition for respondent No.3 and Sri N. Sri Hari,
learned standing counsel for respondent No.5.
3.
Learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that petitioner is absolute owner of the subject property having purchased the same under registered sale deed bearing No.298 of 2000 dated 09.02.2000.
He would submit that the authorities, without following due process of law, are intending to lay road in the petitioner's land, for the convenience of beneficiaries of TIDCO houses.

sentences.text: Learned Assistant Government Pleader for Revenue and Learned Assistant Government Pleader for Land Acquisition would submit that the authorities are not resorting to any highhanded action in respect of the subject property.
SRSJ 5.
Learned standing counsel for respondent No.5 would submit that authorities of Gram Panchayat have undertaken repairs of existing road.
No new road is intended to be laid down.
He would submit that if the authorities intend to lay road and if petitioner's land is required in that connection, the authorities will follow due process of law.

6. Recording the submissions of learned counsel appearing on behalf of the respondents, this writ petition is disposed of directing the respondents not to interfere with the petitioner's possession over the subject property, without following due process of law.
No costs.
As a sequel, pending miscellaneous petitions, if any, shall stand closed.
